name: IN-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Messmer running with a large fundraising edge
No polls or expert ratings; markets price a Democratic win at ~3%
model.rationale: The R+18 district lean, Messmer's incumbency and roughly four-to-one fundraising advantage over Mary Allen all point to a safe Republican hold, and prediction markets agree at about 96% for the GOP. No polling contradicts this picture, so the fundamentals-based margin stands.
model.watch: A late influx of outside spending against Messmer or a polling surprise would be the only realistic path to moving this race toward competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Indiana's 8th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of about 18 points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent Mark Messmer is running for reelection after easily securing his party's nomination, and he holds a decisive financial advantage, having raised roughly $1.2 million to Democrat Mary Allen's $295,000 and entering the fall with about $714,000 on hand.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, but prediction markets give Messmer roughly a 96% chance of winning. With no outside spending on either side and no evidence of a competitive environment, the seat is expected to remain safely in Republican hands.
